candidates.description: The chat route constructs a MongoDB $where query by concatenating user-supplied productId directly into a JavaScript expression string, allowing arbitrary code execution within the MongoDB query context.
candidates.rationale: Line 149 builds `$where: 'this.product == ' + productId` where productId originates from user input. The $where operator evaluates a JavaScript expression server-side, so injecting a payload like `1; sleep(5000)` or `1; this.constructor.constructor('return process')()` achieves code execution. Verification: send a crafted productId with a timing payload and observe response delay.
candidates.title: NoSQL injection via $where operator in chat route

candidates.description: The trackOrder route interpolates user-supplied id into a MongoDB $where JavaScript expression using a template literal, enabling injection of arbitrary JavaScript evaluated by the database.
candidates.rationale: Line 18 uses `$where: \`this.orderId === '${id}'\`` where id comes from req.params or req.query. An attacker can break out of the string literal with a single quote and inject JavaScript. Verification: send id=`x' || '1'=='1` and observe if all orders are returned instead of none.
candidates.title: NoSQL injection via $where operator in trackOrder route

candidates.description: The /dataerasure route is registered with no preceding authentication or authorization middleware, potentially allowing unauthenticated users to trigger data deletion.
candidates.rationale: Route inventory shows /dataerasure has empty middleware_before list, meaning no JWT or session check precedes the handler. The handler likely performs destructive operations (data deletion). Verification: send a POST to /dataerasure without an Authorization header and check if the operation succeeds or returns 401.
candidates.title: Data erasure endpoint mounted without authentication middleware
